ranked_findings.finding: Bulk-refund requests were accepted without idempotency keys, causing duplicate refunds for three enterprise accounts.
evidence: corpus/tickets/TICKET-8729.md: every duplicate has request_class=bulk-refund and no idempotency key
corpus/timeline/incident_timeline.md: duplicate refunds reported at 10:25 UTC

ranked_findings.finding: The idempotency-required guardrail was skipped due to the legacy_batch_header bypass, allowing non-idempotent requests through.
evidence: corpus/timeline/incident_timeline.md: idempotency-required guardrail skipped due to legacy_batch_header at 10:18 UTC

ranked_findings.finding: Single-refund API traffic in the same window included idempotency keys and did not duplicate, isolating the issue to the bulk-refund path.
evidence: corpus/tickets/TICKET-8729.md: Single-refund API traffic in the same window includes idempotency keys and did not duplicate

ranked_findings.finding: Worker replay was an early theory (TICKET-8721) opened before gateway logs were available; final evidence does not support it as the primary trigger.
evidence: corpus/tickets/TICKET-8721.md: Initial theory: queue worker replayed an old payment event after a timeout. This theory was opened before API gateway logs were available.
corpus/remediation/notes.md: Early note: investigate worker replay and retry backoff.

unresolved_ambiguity: Whether the queue worker replay contributed to the incident is not confirmed. TICKET-8721 raised this theory before API gateway logs were available, and the final evidence points to the guardrail skip as the root cause. Worker replay and retry backoff remain an open but unconfirmed secondary concern.
